summary: Sanders County, MT 30-foot timber pole tower built in 1934 for Lolo National Forest; destroyed in 1957, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 30-foot timber pole tower

events.note: 30-foot timber pole tower; sources differ on whether the L-4 cab came with it or was added later
July 1936: Red Goff left the lookout; Wright Harris took his place (newspaper item dated July 15, 1936, reprinted on Forest Lookouts)
July 1937: Bill Alvord stationed at the lookout by the Forest Service (newspaper item dated July 14, 1937, reprinted on Forest Lookouts)
Everett Bean, a UNH junior, reported working for the Forest Service at the lookout (Portsmouth Herald item dated August 7, 1941)
Both sources give 1957 as the year the tower was destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says the L-4 cab was erected with the tower in 1934; firelookout.com says the L-4 cab was added to it later. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. Both give 1934 for the build and 1957 for destruction. The Forest Lookouts page credits the 1957 date to a source it names only as Kresek; I could not identify it, so it is not cited. No source describes what remains at the site today or whether it is open to visitors, so access is left out of facts. The 1941 staffing item is a newspaper report about a letter, so it is thin. Elevation 5,205 ft (about 1,587 m) could fill elevation_m. The record's gone status and 9.1 m height match both sources (30 feet). Used one WebSearch, which returned nothing about the site today. Fact-check 2026-10-10: added dated quotes for the 1936, 1937 and 1941 items, the UNH junior quote and the Sanders County quote.
